pre_conditions: The technician knows the press floor nickname.

uc_name: Review machine history and verify downtime against available machine data
pre_conditions: <mark style="background-color: yellow">The intended machine has been identified; the technician or manager is reviewing diagnosis or downtime.</mark>
flow_of_events: The technician or manager requests recent faults, repairs, and the relevant downtime event.
The system displays what prior shifts tested, changed, and whether the repair held.
The system presents available live readings, run-stop states, cycle counts, alarms, and relevant temperature or pressure history beside technician notes.
If a sensor recorded temperature drift before an alarm, the system shows it beside the repair notes.
The system identifies available machine-data coverage, gaps, and where the technician entry is authoritative.
The worker reviews the evidence for the current task.
For diagnosis, the technician assesses trends, suspect signals, and previous diagnostic attempts.
For downtime review, the manager compares reported downtime with available actual machine states.
Technician records continue to supply diagnosis, repair actions, and downtime reason.
post_conditions: Available history and machine evidence have been reviewed for diagnosis or downtime verification.
non_functional: History and sensor readings should be visible together without hunting through separate screens.
The information should be accessible at the press.
Coverage gaps across machines must be visible.
Sensor data must not replace technician diagnosis and repair records.
alternative_flows: If sensor data are local only or have gaps, the system identifies the unavailable coverage.
<mark style="background-color: yellow">If history is unavailable, the system identifies the missing information rather than implying a complete history.</mark>
<mark style="background-color: yellow">If reported downtime and machine states disagree, the system flags the discrepancy for review; no automatic reconciliation or override rule is assumed.</mark>

uc_name: Record a downtime event, diagnostic work, and repair outcome
pre_conditions: <mark style="background-color: yellow">A machine event has occurred and the intended machine has been identified.</mark>
flow_of_events: The technician logs the machine stop or repair at the machine using the tablet, including a quick note when the cause is found.
The system offers a few simple fields, short prompts, and an adjacent free note.
The system captures downtime in minutes and requires a downtime reason code.
The technician records fault description or code, symptoms, alarms, current machine status, and relevant measurements.
The technician records diagnosis, components tested, test results, and work already attempted.
The technician records corrective actions and changed parts, including part numbers and quantities used.
The technician can add supporting evidence without typing a paragraph.
The technician attaches a photo of the failed part.
Alternatively, the technician records a short voice note.
The technician records whether the repair held through a production run.
The system links technician identity and repair facts to the specific machine event and displays production-order impact.
<mark style="background-color: yellow">The system saves the entry against the selected machine and makes it available in its history.</mark>
If needed, the technician cleans up the initial note later.
post_conditions: The event record contains downtime and reason code, diagnostic and repair facts, and the available verification outcome for subsequent shifts.
non_functional: Entry should be quick at the press with gloves on and shop-floor noise.
Prompts should avoid a long form or extensive mandatory categorization.
Fault codes, part numbers, and corrective actions should remain distinguishable.
Records should be complete and consistent across shifts.
Technical recording must remain separate from production-stop authorization.
alternative_flows: <mark style="background-color: yellow">If a production run has not yet occurred, the record identifies the outcome as not yet verified and the technician updates it after verification.</mark>
<mark style="background-color: yellow">If the reason code is missing, the system prompts before treating the event as complete; enforcement timing needs confirmation.</mark>

<mark style="background-color: yellow">If saving fails, the system reports that the entry has not been saved and allows retry; poor-connectivity handling follows the separate floor-record workflow.</mark>

uc_name: Locate spare parts, record parts use, and manage shortages
pre_conditions: <mark style="background-color: yellow">The machine and component requiring a spare are identified; recording issued parts requires the relevant work order.</mark>
flow_of_events: <mark style="background-color: yellow">The technician requests spare-part information for the machine or failed component.</mark>
The system presents the appropriate spare part and its location.
The next action depends on availability.
If the part is available, the technician uses the location information to retrieve it and records the issued part number and quantity against the work order.
If the part is unavailable, the supervisor marks the machine awaiting parts and escalates according to lead time and production impact.
The manager reviews stock accuracy, stockouts, supplier lead time, downtime waiting for parts, and effects on the production plan.
post_conditions: The technician has available part and location information; issued parts or a shortage and its impact are recorded as applicable.
non_functional: Part and location lookup should be quick during a breakdown.

alternative_flows: <mark style="background-color: yellow">If no matching part or location information is available, the system identifies the information gap; missing data alone is not treated as proof of a stockout.</mark>

pre_conditions: <mark style="background-color: yellow">The technician has a machine-specific troubleshooting technique to consider sharing.</mark>
flow_of_events: <mark style="background-color: yellow">The technician requests or obtains an explanation of who owns shared troubleshooting knowledge and how it will be used.</mark>
<mark style="background-color: yellow">An organization representative explains the applicable ownership and use arrangements.</mark>
<mark style="background-color: yellow">If the technician understands those arrangements and chooses to share, the technician adds the technique to the relevant press note.</mark>

uc_name: Review shift handoff and maintenance job closeout
pre_conditions: A maintenance job is being handed over or proposed for closeout.
flow_of_events: The outgoing technician updates open repairs, temporary fixes, awaited parts, watched machines, and current equipment condition.
For jobs involving isolation, the record identifies energy sources, locks and tags, who applied them and when, isolation ownership, and zero-energy verification.
The system requires critical safety information appropriate to the current job state.
The review follows the job state.
For handoff, the outgoing technician explains the work and the incoming technician reviews the written maintenance and safety record, including isolation ownership and verification.
For closeout, the completed isolation record identifies who released each lock; the supervisor reviews the work, conditions, and documentation.
Incomplete LOTO records are prevented from being handed off or closed.
If information is unclear, the incoming technician contacts the supervisor; if isolation ownership or verification is unclear, work stops rather than guessing.
The supervisor returns incorrect or incomplete information for correction before closeout.
The system records reviewer and closer identity and the corresponding date and time.
post_conditions: An incoming shift receives a complete current safety record, or a completed job has the required supervisor review and closeout evidence.
non_functional: The written record should be a reliable source of truth across shifts.
A handoff must not depend only on verbal updates.
Required release fields must respect ongoing isolation; a handoff is not a release authorization.
alternative_flows: <mark style="background-color: yellow">If required updates are missing, clarification and correction are requested; generic non-safety omissions do not imply an unspecified automatic handover block.</mark>

<mark style="background-color: yellow">If critical records are unavailable during connectivity loss, the workflow remains pending rather than assuming completeness; exact offline authorization rules need confirmation.</mark>

uc_name: Escalate a repair and record a production-stop decision
pre_conditions: There is a safety concern, repeated failure, or no clear repair path.
flow_of_events: The technician stops the work, makes the machine safe, and contacts the supervisor or lead.
The technician records fault, attempted work, status, and escalation reason.
The system routes those facts to the supervisor for an explicit decision.
The supervisor reviews history, manuals, expertise, criticality, safety, repeated failures, parts availability, and production impact.
The supervisor records the next decision.
The repair continues with assigned next steps.
Alternatively, engineering or the supplier is contacted.
Alternatively, an explicit production stoppage is approved.
The supervisor records priority, staffing or production impact, and the approval decision.
If an exception affects plant-wide priorities, major commitments, a critical machine, or resources across shifts, the plant manager reviews and approves the exception.
post_conditions: The escalation and supervisor decision are recorded separately from the technical repair entry.
non_functional: A technician entry alone must not authorize production stoppage.
Decision-making uses criteria rather than an imposed rigid decision tree.
alternative_flows: <mark style="background-color: yellow">If a supervisor decision is pending, the system displays pending approval rather than implying authorization; response deadlines are unspecified.</mark>

pre_conditions: <mark style="background-color: yellow">A repair event is available for release review.</mark>
flow_of_events: The technician records identity, parts replaced, and repair actions for the specific machine event.
The supervisor records who authorized release back into production.
The system records the release decision, approver, and approval time linked to the event.

pre_conditions: <mark style="background-color: yellow">Machine events, statuses, and relevant production-order information are available.</mark>
flow_of_events: The system displays downtime minutes by machine and reason code and highlights repeat failures.
The system displays current status, criticality, order impact, and whether keeping a machine down has supervisor approval.
The manager considers machines currently down or losing the most minutes, especially critical machines tied to an active order.
The manager then considers repeat failures and overdue preventive work along with parts availability, repair time, and technician availability.

The maintenance team checks current production orders and actual availability.
The supervisor coordinates an available maintenance window.
If an urgent order or extended machine run conflicts with the window, the supervisor considers order impact and criticality.

uc_name: Assess the job and record pre-work safety controls
pre_conditions: A maintenance task and equipment are identified.
flow_of_events: The involved workers review job steps, hazards, energy sources, controls, PPE, permits, emergency actions, and responsibilities.
Hazard assessment considers severity, likelihood, and the hierarchy of controls.
The technician identifies all hazardous energy sources, isolates them, applies locks and tags, and verifies zero energy before touching equipment.
The record captures equipment, job, energy sources, completed isolation steps, lock and tag appliers, application times, verifier, and zero-energy verification.

If a critical control is inadequate, the job stops until corrected and verified.

pre_conditions: An unsafe condition or violation is identified.
flow_of_events: Work stops immediately and the people and area are made safe.
The supervisor and EHS are notified before work resumes.
The violation is documented and the control is corrected.
EHS verifies the corrected control before work resumes.

pre_conditions: An event caused harm, damage, or loss, or had the potential to cause harm.

Corrective actions are assigned an owner and due date.

pre_conditions: A chemical spill occurred during maintenance.
flow_of_events: The team stops work and secures or evacuates the affected area until safe.
The event is investigated.
EHS creates a separate environmental report recording material, amount, location, response, and corrective actions.
